1

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 20.04.2021 at about 5.40 pm., when the (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.332/2022 petitioner was riding his bike bearing reg.No.KA-06- HB-3172 near Y.K.Ramaiah Circle on SH-33 i.e., Tumakuru - Kunigal road, at that time, one Luggage Auto bearing reg.No.KA-06-AB-0786 came from Kunigal side at high speed with rash and negligent manner and came to the extreme right to overtake fore going JCB vehicle and caused the accident.
Due to which the petitioner fall down on the road along with his bike and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was taken to CHC, Kunigal for higher treatment he was taken to M.C.Orthopedic Orthoscopy and Joint replacement Center, Tumakuru and admitted as an inpatient.

entities.text: M.C.Orthopedic Orthoscopy and Joint replacement Center, Tumakuru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 22 years and was doing bar bending and centering work and earning Rs.1,200/- to Rs.1,500/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries, (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.332/2022 petitioner has become permanently disabled.
The alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent act of driver of Goods Auto bearing reg.No.KA-06-AB-0786.
The Hebburu police registered a crime against the rider of offending vehicle in CR No.56/2021 under Section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
The respondents being Owner and Insurer of the Luggage Auto bearing reg.No.KA-06-AB-0786 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, petitioner constrained to file a petition for compensation.
3. After service of notice the respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through respective counsel and filed their written statement.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is as under:
(SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.332/2022
Respondent contended that, the luggage Auto bearing reg.No.KA-06-AB-0786 was insured with respondent No.2 and policy was in force at the time of alleged accident covering all risks.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, excessive and without any legal basis.
Further contended that, the driver of the vehicle was having valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
With this ground he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is as under:
This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the Luggage Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AB-0786 and liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and subject to valid and effective driving license of the driver.

2 respondent has denied the contents of claim petition (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.332/2022 specifically and categorically.

sentences.text: It has specifically denied the manner of accident, the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.

It has also denied the injuries sustained,
treatment taken and expenses incurred towards medicine.

It has contended that,
owner/1st respondent of luggage auto has not submitted the claim form and other documents like RC, DL and permit etc., for verification.
Further contended that there was a delay in lodging the complaint.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
With this ground it has prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioner proves that, on 20.04.2021 when he was going towards his native village Lakkannagowdanapalya side from (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.332/2022 Hebbur side by riding his motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-06-HB-3172, at about 5.40 pm., near Y.K.Ramaiah Circle on SH-33 i.e., Tumakuru - Kunigal Road at that time Luggage Auto bearing No.KA-06-AB-0786 was came from Kunigal side in very high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed against him and he sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum ?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and got marked document at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10, Dr. S.A.Somashekara was examined as PW2 and got marked document at Ex.P11 &
12.
On behalf of respondent No.2 it examined its Senior Legal Executive as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 3 and closed their evidence.
6. Heard arguments of learned counsel for (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.332/2022 petitioner and respondents.

The learned counsel for petitioner has submitted citations reported in:
1) MFA No.8602/2016 2) MVC No.1794/2018 3) CA No.2567/2020 d) CA No.5123/2019 Madhu vs Abdul Razzaq on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199557314/
3 e) CA No.8510/2022.
7.

sentences.text:
My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2: Party in the Affirmative; Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
-:R E A S O N S:-
8.

Issue No.1:- It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 20.04.2021 at about 5.40 pm., when the petitioner was riding his bike bearing reg.No.KA- (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.332/2022 06-HB-3172 near Y.K.Ramaiah Circle on SH-33 i.e., Tumakuru - Kunigal road, at that time, one Luggage Auto bearing reg.No.KA-06-AB-0786 came from Kunigal side at high speed with rash and negligent manner and came to the extreme right to overtake fore going JCB vehicle and caused the accident.
Due to which the petitioner fall down on the road along with his bike and sustained injuries.
9. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination by reiterating all the facts mentioned in the petition.
He also relied documents at Ex.P1 to P10.
The Ex.P1 is the FIR and complaint, Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.3 is the IMV report, Ex.P.4 is the wound certificate, Ex,P.5 is the charge sheet and Ex.P.6 is the discharge summary.

Ex.P.7 is the prescriptions, Ex.P.8 is the medical bills, Aadhar card (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.332/2022 and Pan card.
10.

I have perused Ex.P.1 to 5 which shows that petitioner himself has lodged complaint and on the basis of the same, Hebbur police have registered the case in Cr.No.0056/2021 for the offence punishable U/ Sec.279 & 337 of IPC on 22.04.2021 at 14.00.

Thereafter, the Investigating Officer had conducted the Investigation and filed the Charge Sheet against the driver of the Luggage auto by name Abdul Razak for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
11.
The PW1/petitioner has stated the cause of the accident in his chief-examination affidavit.
The PW1 was subjected to cross-examined but nothing was elicited to disbelieve the evidence of PW1 with regard to accident.
The Respondent No.2 though contended that the alleged Luggage auto was not involved in the accident.
But prove this aspect, the respondent No.2 (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.332/2022 has not led any evidence.
Moreover the Ex.P3 - IMV Report discloses that the damages caused to both vehicle.
The 2nd respondent only denied the case of the petitioner.

Apart from this in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal case.

This principles of law was laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others).
Madhu vs Abdul Razzaq on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199557314/
4 12.
The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent tried to elicited in the cross-examination of PW1 that there is a delay in lodging the complaint.
Since the injured has sustained severe injuries and as such we cannot expect to lodge the complaint by the injured soon after the accident.
Normally, injured person will (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.332/2022 give preference to take treatment rather than compliance of legal requirements.
Same has been done by the petitioner in this case.
Therefore, the question of delay losses its significance.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in a reported decision (2011) 4 SCC 693 Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that - " It is well settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian Conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after the accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of the kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so,
the contents of FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.332/2022 has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons, then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the Police to initiate investigation of Criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves the factum of accident, so that victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay is doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.
Therefore, the documents relied by petitioner and oral evidence of PW1 clearly establishes that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence act of the driver of Luggage auto.
Now it can safely be concluded, that the injuries were caused to the petitioner due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.

Therefore,
I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved issue No.1.
Hence, I answered issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.332/2022 compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant,
charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc. let me discuss one by one:
a) TOWARDS INJURY, PAIN AND SUFFERING:
Madhu vs Abdul Razzaq on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199557314/
5
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and discharged with an advise to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove injuries caused to him he has produced wound certificate/Ex.P4,
which reveals that petitioner has sustained simple as well as grievous injuries.

The record also shows that the petitioner took treatment in the hospital as an inpatient and the (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.332/2022 petitioner has examined doctor by name Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW2 to prove the disability.
The PW.2 got marked documents at Ex.P11 & 12.
The PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner.
Therefore by considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at hospital and produced 31 prescriptions at Ex.P.7 and 50 medical bills marked at Ex.P8 for Rs.1,91,719/-.
During cross examination of PW.1, learned counsel for respondent No.2 has disputed the bill No.50 amounting to Rs.1,10,150/-.
But with regard to that suggestion respondent has not taken any steps (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.332/2022 to prove the same.
Rather, there is no dispute about these medical bills, the Tribunal is of the view that petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,91,719/- is just and reasonable towards Medical Expenses.
c) TOWARDS FOOD, EXTRA NOURISHMENT, CONVEYANCE AND MEDICAL ATTENDANT CHARGES
: On perusal of Ex.P.6 - discharge summary it shows that the petitioner took treatment as inpatient at M.C.Orthopaedic Centre from 20.04.2021 to 02.05.2021 i.e., for a period of 13 days.
During the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/-
per day for 13 days and also by including conveyance it is just and reasonable to award Rs.20,000/-
towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.332/2022 attendant.
d) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner contended that he was doing bar bending and centering work and earning Rs.1,200/- to Rs.1,500/- pm, as a income.
In order to prove his income he has not produced any documents to show that he was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income this Tribunal will consider notional income.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2021 at 15,000/- p.m.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2021 treated as Rs.15,000/- p.m.,
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case this tribunal held that petitioner is entitled to Rs.30,000/- = (Rs.15,000/- x 2) towards loss of income during laid up period.

(SCCH-9) 18 MVC.No.332/2022 Madhu vs Abdul Razzaq on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199557314/
6 e) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he was inpatient in the hospital and has become permanently disabled.
The petitioner also examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara working as an Orthopeadic Surgeon, at Bowring Hospital, Bengaluru as PW2.

This PW2 deposed that petitioner came to their hospital with history of RTA and diagnosed to have Grade III Open right patella comminuted fracture, right lateral plateau comminuted and right tibia and fibula shaft fracture, right femur lateral condyle fracture and open fracture right 3 rd metacarpal.

He underwent surgery in the form of debridement, ORIF right femoral condyle with CC screws, right tibial plateau and shaft with LCP (10 holed), patellectomy, patellar tendon repair all under SA, percutaneous K-Wire fixation to 3rd metacarpal.

On presentation he complains pain and difficulty in (SCCH-9) 19 MVC.No.332/2022 walking and climbing stairs, inability to squat and sit cross legged, deformed and shortened limb, inability to work as a Bar Bender and Centering worker and inability to bend right hand 3rd finger.

On examination PW.2 noticed, the petitioner walks with pain and limping, wasting of right thigh, diffuse swelling of right leg and vorus deformity of right knee is seen, shortening of right lower limb is seen, surgical and secondary scars are seen over right knee and leg and right MCP joint.

Recent X-ray shows united fracture distal femur right with implants in situ, non visualization of patella right, united fracture proximal tibia and shaft of tibia,
non union fracture proximal fibula and malunited # mid shaft fibula and malunited # 3rd metacarpal right hand.
PW.2 assessed total disability of both limbs at 66% and 33% at whole body.
As per wound certificate Ex.P6
the doctor has (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.332/2022 opined that the injury No.1 to 4 are simple in nature and injury No.5 to 9 are grievous in nature.
The PW2/ Doctor has assessed the total disability of both limbs at 66% and to the whole body at 33%.
PW2 has also produced out patient record and one X-ray which are marked at ExP11 & 12 respectively.
During his cross examination PW.2 has deposed that, he has not treated the petitioner and admitted that, the femur and tibia fractures are united, implants are in situ.
It is material to note that during the course of cross-examination there is nothing to elicit from the mouth to disbelieve the evidence of PW.2 about assessment of disability.
The petitioner contended that he was doing Bar Bending work.
The PW.2 assessed the whole body disability at 33%.

Therefore considering avocation of the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and considering the evidence of PW.2 and all the (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.332/2022 aspects available on record the disability is assessed at 20%.
In order to prove the age of the petitioner he has produced Ex.P.9 - Aadhar card.
On persual of the same, the petitioner was born on 23.09.1999 and date of accident was 20.04.2021.
Hence the age of the petitioner is taken into consideration 22 years for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "18" is applicable as per Smt. Sarala Verma's case.
As per the ratio laid down in Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar and anr, this Tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his income.

sentences.text: As already stated above the petitioner has not produced any document to prove his income and in the absence of positive documents about salary the notional income has to be considered.

Hence,
future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
(SCCH-9) 22 MVC.No.332/2022 15,000 x 12 x 18 x 12/100 = Rs.3,88,800/- The petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,88,800/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
f) Towards Deprivation Of Future Amenities:
Madhu vs Abdul Razzaq on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199557314/
7
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he can't carry out his work/any manual work.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.10,000/- is just and reasonable towards under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
g) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The doctor PW2 has opined that the petitioner is required Rs.50,000/- for future medical expenses i.e., for removal of implants in situ in private set up.
But the doctor has not produced any estimation cost for the (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.332/2022 future medical expenses to the petitioner as he admitted during his cross examination.
The petitioner claiming Rs.50,000/- for future medical expenses.

However, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the injuries sustained by the petitioner I am of the view that an amount of Rs.10,000/- is just and reasonable towards future medical expenses.

14. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

Total compensation .7,00,519/-
15.
Regarding Liability:
As already stated above the petitioner has proved that the accident in question was caused by the driver of the luggage auto bearing reg.No.KA-06-AB-0786 with rash and negligent driving act.
The respondent No.2 has admitted issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect said luggage auto but it has contended that the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

The respondent No.2 argued that, luggage auto has not holding valid RC Madhu vs Abdul Razzaq on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199557314/
8 and permit.

Further respondent Insurance company has examined its Senior Legal Executive as RW.1 and through him got marked 3 documents such as authorisation letter, policy and (SCCH-9)
25 MVC.No.332/2022 Driving licence of driver of offending luggage auto bearing reg.No.KA-06-AB-0786.
During his cross examination he has admitted that policy was in force at the time of accident and also admitted that his insured vehicle has been charge sheeted.
Further contended that, he had non transport licence.
On going through the cross examination it came to know that, there is no material to show that the respondent No.1 has violated the policy conditions.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on (SCCH-9) 26 MVC.No.332/2022 the above said issues, the tribunal proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .7,00,519/- (Rupees seven lakhs five hundred and nineteen Only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(Future medical expenses shall not carry any interest).
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said  (SCCH-9) 27 MVC.No.332/2022  compensation amount, 50% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 50% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper verification an identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer over computer directly, corrected and pronounced by me in open court on this 6th day of February, 2025.)
